title: The 1688 Germantown protest asks how Christians can sell a person as a slave for life
summary: The 1688 Germantown protest asks how a person can be sold as a slave for life.
body: The Germantown resolutions ask whether it is right to sell a person or make him a slave for all the time of his life, and they compare the fear of being sold by Turks. The protest is a local Quaker and Mennonite petition against the slave trade in Pennsylvania. It did not end slavery there. The wording on the page includes: "as followeth: Is there any that would be done or handled at this manner? viz., to be sold or made a slave for all the time of his life? How fearful and faint-hearted are many at sea, when they see a strange vessel, being afraid it should be a Turk, and they should be taken, and sold for slaves into Turkey. Now, what is this better done, than Turks do? Yea, rather it is worse for them".

sources.title: Resolutions of the Germantown Mennonites, 18 February 1688
sources.author: Avalon Project, Yale Law School
